summary: Fang-Kuei Li worked in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. He earned his BA at Michigan and PhD at Chicago under Sapir, Bloomfield, and Buck. He taught at Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at Lancaster University in 2008. They served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Farzand Ali Durrani was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab, the University of Peshawar (~1952–1954), and the University of London (~1961–1964), later serving as professor at Peshawar (~1970–1993).

Fausta Nowotny was an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner (~1938–1942). She worked as a staff member (Mitarbeiterin) at the Weltmuseum Wien from 1943 to 1951.

Fausto Ghirardini Fumi worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Giuseppe Bardelli and at Pisa, Florence, and Leipzig. He taught at the University of Palermo (1887–1890) before becoming an ordinary professor at the University of Genoa in 1890.

Fawad Khan is a scholar in archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, serving as assistant curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums (attested 2022).

Fazun was a Buddhist and Tibetan studies scholar who studied under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and others, attending Drepung Monastery (~1926–1930). He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies (1933) and served as vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Federica Venturi is a scholar in tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Indiana University Bloomington in 2013, where she was also an editor (attested 2004), and joined the CRCAO as associate researcher in 2021.

Federico Squarcini is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He became a professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2011 and has served as a series editor for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012).

Felix Hartmann was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen (PhD ~1877–1881) under Jacob Wackernagel. He served as Oberlehrer at Preußische Hauptkadettenanstalt (1884) and docent at Berlin (1906–1935).

Felix Solmsen was a linguist who studied under Johannes Schmidt in Berlin and earned his PhD at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served as Privatdozent (1893) and extraordinary professor (1897) at the University of Bonn.

Feng Youlan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and Columbia University. He held posts at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1946–1947).

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen and Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and later held a post at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.
Ferdinand Hahn worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Gossner Mission School in 1865 and served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church beginning in 1869.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a religious studies and linguistics scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829). He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Marburg and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Heinrich Ewald, and Johann Gildemeister, later serving as professor (from 1869) and rector (1887–1888) at Marburg.

Ferdinand Lessing was a scholar of sinology, tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Berlin. He held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1928–1935) and as Agassiz Professor at UC Berkeley (1935–1949).

Ferdinand Masing was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu (1868–1869) and earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig (1874–1878) under August Leskien, Georg Curtius, Heinrich Hübschmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Karl Brugmann.

Ferdinand Sommer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Freiburg and habilitated at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD 1880 under Ernst Windisch). He served as Maître de Conférences at the EPHE (1881–1891) and professor at the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
